chapter_theme: The fifth part of Pambatti's kummi to the snake turns from attacking outward religion to the inner method itself: the world is false and the root alone worth knowing, merit and penance are void without the Lord's feet, and in a long run of eight-foot stanzas the snake is shut in the body's pot, raised through the sushumna and the letters of the five-syllable mantra, and set dancing in the open space, ending in silence and the end of birth.
structure_note: Ten four-line kummi stanzas (2080 to 2090) on knowledge, devotion and renunciation are followed by fifteen eight-line எண்சீர் விருத்தம் stanzas (2091 to 2104) that are almost wholly cipher: letters, pots, pillars, ships, a gun, smithies and the snake's dance. Several open with the formula 'we will shut the snake in the ... pot' (2096, 2104), continued in chapter 107. Every stanza ends in ஆடாய் பாம்பே; the readings give what each stanza adds.

2080.reading: If one knows the root, one can see all three worlds beforehand and reach eternal release; is there any gain in knowing a great many roots? Be clear that the world is false, and dance.
2080.nuance: The plain contrast is one root against many: knowing the single source against a herbalist's or scholar's knowledge of countless roots. மூலவேர் can also point to the root-centre (மூலம்) of the yogic body. சகத்தைப் பொய் is the Vedantic world-is-false, said flatly.

2081.reading: They do not say the world is beginningless but say the beginningless one made it; they do not know the Real. Say that apart from the power of the great state of kalpa there is no other power, and dance.
2081.nuance: The first two lines can be read as Pambatti holding, against those who teach creation, that the world is itself beginningless, or as mocking anyone who argues about origins while ignorant of சத்து, the Real. The second would sit better with 2080's world-is-false. மகத்துவ நிலைகற்பம் sets the kalpa, the deathless state or preparation, above every other power.

2082.reading: The Siddha seated in the house of a thousand and eight petals, the wondrous Siddha who fills the whole cosmos, the causal Siddha who grows high without a body, has become the light within the eye.
2082.nuance: The thousand-petalled lotus at the crown (here a thousand and eight) is the seat; the same one fills all the அண்டம் and is the light in the eye, so the crown, the cosmos and the eye are one place. The Lord is called a சித்தன், a Siddha, in the Siddhars' own title.

2083.reading: If one sets uppermost the Lord whose form is letters, sought at the centre of the forty-three-angled state, all the upper worlds become servants to his soft feet.
2083.nuance: நாற்பத்துமுக்கோணம் is read by tradition as the forty-three triangles of the Sri Chakra, at whose centre the deity sits; அக்கரச் சொரூபம் makes the Lord a body of letters, the mantra itself. Without that key the number is only a diagram.

2084.reading: Those who have seen never tell, and those who tell have never seen; those who wear an assumed costume do not see the King's state; dance and dance.
2084.nuance: The first two lines are the Siddhar proverb கண்டவர் விண்டிலர், விண்டவர் கண்டிலர். The third adds the costume: the ascetic's outward garb is one more way of telling without seeing.

2085.reading: Before the one who dances inside the hut of six kalas goes off to the neighbouring house, build a fort round him; once he has parted, it is hard to bring him back; hold him close and do not let him go.
2085.nuance: The dancer in the hut is the life or breath in the body; the neighbouring house is death or another body. ஆறுகலைக் குச்சு may be the body of six centres or of six kalas. The plain sense is to guard life while it is here; the coded sense is to hold the breath within.

2086.reading: What use is doing every one of the countless merits, if the heart does not think of the One's feet? Be sure that without devotion the fruit of hard penance comes to ruin.
2086.nuance: The verse does not reject merit or penance but makes them void without பத்தி; பாழ்படும் (goes to waste, to the void) is a strong word for the Siddhars, who elsewhere use பாழ் for the highest emptiness.

2087.reading: What is gained if every world becomes one's own, when one does not think of our Lord's lotus feet? Thinking that this worldly life may be cut off today, remember the Maker's feet and dance.

2088.reading: You put on the wedding finery, rejoiced greatly and stood bewildered with children, house and kin; if even after seeing the corpse's finery you do not renounce, it is only a companion to birth.
2088.nuance: மணக்கோலம் and பிணக்கோலம், the bridal array and the corpse's array, rhyme: the same body is dressed twice. The verse blames not marriage but failing to renounce after seeing death.

2089.reading: I will tell you one great medicine to cut off both birth and death, so hear it eagerly: know the way to open with the key the lock of the mind and the door of thought, and dance.
2089.nuance: The great medicine (பெருமருந்து) is not a drug but a knowing; the lock and door are the mind's, so the release is an opening of the mind rather than an escape from the body.

2090.reading: The five who died were the ones he loved; tell everyone that they have died; and stand and dance so that those on earth may know the way, saying that the one who forgot is one.
2090.nuance: The five dead are most likely the five senses (or the five airs) killed in practice, and he who loved them the self; மறந்தவர் ஒருவர் may be the one who has forgotten the world. The syntax is loose and the stanza may be damaged; this reading is a guess.

2091.reading: Becoming a snake at the root of ஆ, spreading its hood in the field of bliss, folding in at the root of ஊ, running and stretching out the tongue of வ: when the Siddha snake-charmer taught the mantra in which சீ lay, we cut the root of birth in ம and passed beyond maya's bonds.
2091.nuance: The syllables are the cipher: ஆ, ஊ and ம give the pranava's a, u and m, and வ and சீ the letters of சிவ in the five-letter mantra. Tradition takes the snake as the coiled power rising through the syllables. சித்தப்பிடாரனார், the Siddha snake-charmer, is the guru and also Pambatti's own name.

2092.reading: Those who speak tantra know [only] themselves; those who speak the single mantra do not know its meaning; mantra-chanters circle the wall inside the round house and do not find the gate. Go up into the sky, pull up the root, make a pill with the knowledge called grace: if you eat this medicine there is no more birth.
2092.nuance: The first line is ambiguous: தம்மை அறிவார் may be sarcastic (they know only themselves) or a real concession. The second half borrows the herbalist's procedure (pull the root, roll the pill) for an inner one: the root is pulled in the sky, the binding agent is grace.

2093.reading: Building a ship of clay, setting up a heavy mast for all to see, making the field of the senses the rudder, hoisting the sail of the support called knowledge, holding it within the circle called space and sailing it to conquer the sea of Vedanta: the ship the clear-minded jnani sails has reached the holy feet.
2093.nuance: The clay ship is the body, the clay of 2039's potter. அளிபுலம் and சீனி (sail, or saddle as in 2057) are uncertain words. Vedanta is here a sea to be crossed and conquered, where in 2067 it was a landing-place.

2094.reading: One must feel within the heart, know both the inner and the outer, slowly rouse the fire, drive it into the water of the street, drive off the thieving senses, stand seeing above the nose between the eyes, seek the clear supreme light: we have seen the holy feet.
2094.nuance: கனலை எழுப்ப (rouse the fire) is the waking of the inner heat or kundalini; கண்ணுக்கு மூக்குமேல் is the gaze fixed above the nose between the brows. வீதிப் புனல் (the water of the street) is obscure, perhaps the channel along which the fire is sent.

2095.reading: On the summit of the pillar of Om, know both inner and outer; cutting off egoism and anger, damming the flood of bliss, joined firmly to the Steadfast One beyond the hour of death, calm, sleeping without sleeping and reaching ease, dance saying thonthom.
2095.nuance: ஓங்காரக் கம்பம் is the spine or central channel taken as Om, the pillar of 2063. தூங்காமல் தூங்கி, sleeping without sleep, is the Siddhars' phrase for samadhi. தாணு (Sthanu, the immovable) is Siva.

2096.reading: We will shut the snake in the pot of longing, set it dancing in the open space of Vedanta, pluck out the causes and feed them to it, make it dance standing in the harsh expanse of time; mounting the horse and circling the whole old world, seeing the eternal subtlety and reciting the mantra beyond words, we brought it back and gained the four.
2096.nuance: விரகக் குடம் may be the pot of passion or of separation: the body. The horse (துரகம்) is the breath. ஒருநான்கும் is unexplained: tradition might take it as the four kinds of release or the four aims of life. உரையற்ற மந்திரம், the mantra without words, anticipates 2104's swallowed letter.

2097.reading: Letting the snake that stood in the body-pot wander in the sea of compassion, driving it far through the loving sushumna, seeking to fix the eternal Thing, climbing the vast space of maya and searching to attain the stainless Thing, we crossed the landing of the ... and joined the bliss of the void beyond.
2097.nuance: The stages run body, compassion, sushumna, maya's space and the void beyond (அப்பால் பாழ்): the highest state is called பாழ், emptiness. ஆயத் துறை is unclear: a toll-landing, or the landing of the tattvas.

2098.reading: Taking the thought that stood at the root place up through the whole sushumna to the bindu-circle in the upper place, it lives on that path; by the compassion of the holy young mother, becoming the form of knowledge of the supreme state, standing with Mal who sleeps on the banyan leaf, we joined bliss.
2098.nuance: The movement is from the root (மூலம்) to the bindu at the head. பாலத் திருத்தாய் may be the young mother, the Vaalai of the Siddhars, or a mother of milk. Vishnu asleep on the banyan leaf is an unusual figure here, perhaps for the mind dissolved in cosmic sleep. வேலை வழி (the sea's way or the way of the task) is unclear.

2099.reading: Making one the mind, the horse that gallops in the street of the five senses, crossing the worlds bound by mala, seeking the state of the abiding guru's feet: crossing the five places and the earth is crossing the moon's sphere too; leaving the troubled sea of this earth, become bliss and dance.
2099.nuance: The horse is the mind again, as in 2057; here it is not bridled but made one-pointed (ஒருமைப்படுத்தி). The five places and the moon's sphere are read by tradition as the lower adharas and the moon-centre in the head.

2100.reading: Taking the form of the teacher called guru, making the aimed knowledge the gun and grace itself the bullet, going beyond it in bliss, firing at the mind's path of the women called delusion so that it burns without coming back, saying it struck within the great ring, hold to the one who holds to nothing and dance.
2100.nuance: The gun (துப்பாக்கி) and bullet (உண்டை) are rare in this corpus and show the stanza's lateness. பற்றானைப் பற்றி, hold to the one without holding, is the Kural's paradox in two words. மருளென்னு மாதர் may mean the women who are delusion, or delusion as a woman.

2101.reading: We will stop the wind in the coppersmith's cave, kindle fire in the blacksmith's forge, make gold on the head of those who spoke, make learning equal ... ; we will burn away the bond of women, see the mark of the true Thing and reach what we desired; not babbling, not babbling, staying still, we joined Parapara.
2101.nuance: கால் is both leg and wind: stopping it in the cave is the breath held. The smithy and gold-making are the alchemist's tools, which the stanza may mean literally or as inner work. Line four is obscure. The close, பன்னாதே, சும்மா இருந்து, puts silence above all the furnace-work.

2102.reading: We will set fire to the divisions of caste, plant a pole in the open market, play at the branching of the streets, make kinship in the house we should not, search and roam and then fall asleep, and delight in the pleasing woman: the five primal Brahmas do not know this.
2102.nuance: Read plainly the stanza flaunts transgression: burning caste, entering forbidden houses, enjoying a woman. Read in the Siddhars' cipher the streets are the nadis, the woman is Vaalai or Shakti, and the sleep is yogic. Both readings stand; the first line at least is plain. The five Brahmas may be the five deities over the elements.

2103.reading: Taking our stand on the long letter, twisting the tail on the letter that does not leave, spreading the hood on that released letter, moving and dancing on the way of the sky, settling even on the struck letter, gathering in the twelfth letter, we joined the holy feet of the preceptor who firmly gave us grace.
2103.nuance: The stanza is a ladder of letters: நெட்டெழுத்து (long vowel), the unleaving letter, the letter let go, the twelfth letter (ஔ is the twelfth vowel, or the twelve finger-breadths of breath). No key in the text fixes which letters are meant.

2104.reading: We will shut the snake in the pot with a needle's hole, roam round the whole world, forget the stained birth, set it dancing in the space where the mind agrees, feed it the stained senses as prey, climb and dance on the summit the mind has reached, and swallow even the spoken letter: we are free of birth and death.
2104.nuance: The pot with a needle's hole is the body, perhaps its narrow opening at the crown. பேசும் எழுத்தையும் விழுங்கி, swallowing the letter that speaks, takes the practice past mantra into silence, the end that the letter-stanzas lead to.

links.note: Tirumular calls the teaching beyond the tattvas one that cannot be told, and adds that if it is told it is Siva the Supreme; Pambatti says flatly that those who tell have not seen. Both hold the truth to be untellable, but Tirumular leaves room for a telling that is itself the Lord.

Valluvar asks what learning has achieved if the learned do not bow at the feet of the one of pure knowledge; Pambatti asks what all merits achieve if the heart does not think of the One's feet. The same 'what use' question, with merit and penance in place of learning.

Sangili Siddhar and Pambatti both set மணக்கோலம் against பிணக்கோலம், the wedding array against the corpse's array, in a household of wife and children. Sangili mocks the one who does not know it will come; Pambatti blames the one who has seen it and still does not renounce.

The Naladiyar's wedding drums become funeral drums for the bridegroom on the same day; Pambatti's wedding finery becomes the corpse's finery. Both use the one body dressed for marriage and for burning, and both draw renunciation from it.

Both name a great medicine (மாமருந்து, பெருமருந்து) that is no drug: for Tirumular it is the Lord's pair of feet, for Pambatti the knowing of how the mind's lock opens. One finds the medicine in grace received, the other in an act of knowing.

Tirumular calls false gurus those who have looked over mantra and tantra but do not reflect on them; Pambatti says those who speak the single mantra do not know its meaning and that mantra-chanters circle the wall without finding the gate. Both separate handling the mantra from knowing it.

Within Pambatti's own song: the wooden ship of ten nadis, ten airs and seven dhatus lurches and falls, and the reader is told to sail the fitting ship on the one flood; here the clay ship steered by knowledge crosses the sea of Vedanta to the feet. The body is the ship both times, first doomed and then rightly sailed.

Bathiragiriyar longs to launch the ship of love on the sea of knowledge; Pambatti's ship has knowledge for its sail and crosses the sea of Vedanta. The ship and sea are shared, but the cargo differs: love in one, knowledge in the other.

Tirumular gazes steadily at the space between the brows and finds there the Supreme's seat; Pambatti stands looking above the nose between the eyes and seeks the supreme light. The same gaze practice, with the same thing found at its end.

Pattinathar confesses that not keeping his eyes open on the tip of the nose spoiled his body and understanding; Pambatti tells the practitioner to stand looking above the nose. The same fixed gaze, regretted as neglected in one and prescribed in the other.

In 2063 the golden pillar in the middle street is garlanded with no key given; here the pillar is named the pillar of Om and the practitioner stands on its summit. The later stanza supplies the cipher the earlier one left open.

Both make the mind a horse: in 2057 it is bridled with the intellect and ridden to clarity, here it gallops in the street of the five senses and is made one-pointed. The same image from control to concentration.

Valluvar tells the reader to cling to the clinging of the one who has no clinging; Pambatti ends his stanza with பற்றானைப் பற்றி, holding to the one who holds nothing. The same paradox, compressed into two words.

Agappei says to stay still, that the formula has been told and the place of stillness is what was pointed to; Pambatti, after the forge and the gold-making, says that by not babbling and staying still he joined Parapara. Both put சும்மா இரு, simply being still, at the end of the method.

In 2078 caste differences belong to worldlings and not to true sadhus; here the poet will set fire to caste divisions and go into the houses he should not. The earlier stanza says the realised are untouched by caste; this one acts against it.

source_issues: 2090: the stanza's syntax is loose (இறந்தவர் ஐவரவர் இட்ட மானவர் / எய்தும்அவ ரிறந்தாரென்று) and may be damaged.
2093: அளிபுலந் and சீனி are unclear and may be corrupt.
2097: ஆயத் துறை in line 7 is obscure.
2101: line 4 (கருதி யருகல்வி ஒப்பஞ் செய்வோம்) does not parse cleanly and looks damaged.
